title: `any` stays usable in authored .sm: the language does not forbid it
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Dynamic Features': '`any` and `eval` remain usable. General Smithers guidance may lint against them; the language does not forbid them.' The correct observable behavior is that the program compiles and runs — a compiler that rejected `any` outright would fail this case, and specification/compatibility.mdx §4 forbids invalidating TypeScript escape hatches. WITHDRAWAL (2026-08-23): this case previously pinned the second bucket of the portable / `TypeScript`-required / forbidden classification, citing 'Use of any and eval MUST contribute TypeScript.' That classification and the `TypeScript` requirement are withdrawn — 'There is no portable / `TypeScript`-required / forbidden classification, because there is no second target to be portable to' — so the case now pins only the half of the old sentence the specification kept: `any` is not forbidden. The observable is unchanged; only the citation moved. RE-SCOPED 2026-09-01 by migration step 14, and the observable is again unchanged. `any` is still not forbidden and this program still compiles and runs — what narrowed is one position, not the escape hatch. A receiver typed `any` in a position where the analysis must decide CALLABILITY is now treated as callable, so `(value as any).constructor` is SMITHERS1604 where it used to compile with an empty row; see 20-host-globals/an-any-receivers-constructor-is-dynamic-code-evaluation. This case is deliberately left byte-identical rather than extended, because its job is the half of the sentence the specification kept — '`any` and `eval` remain usable ... the language does not forbid them' — and `${value}` on an `any` parameter is exactly that half. Widening it to cover the new refusal would merge the permission and the narrowing into one case, and the next reader could no longer tell which of the two a red run had broken.
